title: A Spire for the Oath
premise: Sebastian Reyes, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a ledger-keeper in the Meridian Guild of impossible trades, discovers the guild's oldest debt: a covenant between the mortal realm and the star-realm, renewed each century at the Spire of Vows. When the border wards collapse and the stars extinguish on the same night, Sebastian learns the guild's master sold the covenant's keystone to buy the guild's survival decades ago. Hunted by the guild's enforcers and shadowed by Ilse Vane, the warden who once loved them and now serves the dying wards, Sebastian must gather the scattered fragments of the keystone and climb the Spire to speak the oath anew. In the end, Sebastian reforges the covenant by surrendering their own storm-gift and memories of exile as payment, choosing love and duty over the invisibility that kept them alive.
about_author: Felix Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trade ledgers in port cities, a habit that bleeds into every novel. They write fantasy about people whose debts, magical and mortal, always come due.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A quiet night cataloguing impossible trades in the Meridian Guild: bottled thunder, a borrowed shadow, a promise with interest. Sebastian's storm-gift flickers when they touch a ledger entry marked with the Spire's sigil, and they bury the reaction. Emotional beat: the fragile comfort of a carefully hidden life, already cracking at the seams.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The border wards shatter and every star vanishes within the same hour. Panic floods the city; the guild locks its doors, and Master Corvane orders the ledgers sealed. Sebastian recognizes the Spire sigil burning on the guild's foundation stone. Emotional beat: dread and a terrible sense of recognition—the catastrophe feels like a debt being called.

chapters.title: A Visitor from the Warden's Watch
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Warden Ilse Vane arrives to investigate the wards' collapse and finds Sebastian's name in an old ward-log. Their reunion is cold, professional, and charged with the history of the exile she was ordered to enforce. She needs a storm-caller; Sebastian needs to stay hidden. Emotional beat: old love curdled into wary alliance.

chapters.title: The Debt Beneath the Guild
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, with Corvane present. Sebastian breaks into the guild's sealed archive and finds the covenant's original terms—and proof that Corvane sold the keystone fragment forty years ago to keep the guild solvent during a famine. Corvane catches them and confesses, unrepentant. Emotional beat: the sickening discovery that survival was purchased with the world's safety.

chapters.title: What the Dark Trades
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. With the stars gone, starless things slip through the broken wards and begin trading in the city's markets, buying memories. Ilse watches a child sell her mother's face for bread. She and Sebastian realize the fragments of the keystone are being bought up by something ancient. Emotional beat: horror at what darkness prices, and what people pay.

chapters.title: Three Fragments, One Road
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Sebastian and Ilse track two keystone fragments: one in a debtors' prison, one in the hands of a memory-broker. They bargain, steal, and nearly die, and Ilse learns Sebastian's exile was engineered by Corvane to keep them from the Spire. Emotional beat: trust rebuilt through shared danger, love rekindled against both their judgments.

chapters.title: The Price of the Third Piece
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The final fragment is held by the thing that bought it: a starless entity wearing the shape of Sebastian's dead mentor. It offers a trade—the fragment for Sebastian's storm-gift, the source of their exile and their identity. Ilse begs them to refuse. Sebastian accepts. Emotional beat: sacrifice as both wound and liberation.

chapters.title: Corvane's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. As the city darkens, the guild's enforcers turn on Corvane, and the guild's own contracts begin collecting on him—his memories, his name, his guild. He dies clutching a ledger, realizing too late that he was the debt. Sebastian and Ilse escape the collapsing guild with the fragments. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in full, without redemption.

chapters.title: The Spire of Vows
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The climb through starless dark, the fragments refusing to join until a speaker offers something true. The entity from chapter seven returns to claim its interest: Sebastian's memories of exile—every year of hiding, every ledger, the person they became. Sebastian speaks the old oath and pays. Emotional beat: the climax, love witnessed at the edge of erasure.

chapters.title: A Ledger with Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The stars return; the covenant holds. Sebastian wakes with the storm-gift gone and the exile-years hollowed out, remembering Ilse only as a stranger who wept at their bedside. Ilse chooses to stay and help them write new memories rather than restore old ones. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—survival's price paid, and a love beginning again from a blank page.
